'''Brian Garner Wybourne''' (5 March 1935 – 26 November 2003) was a New Zealand theoretical physicist known for his groundbreaking work on the energy levels of rare-earth ions and applications of [[Lie group]]s to the atomic ''f'' shell and by mathematicians for his work on group representation theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Butler |first1=Phillip H |last2=King |first2=Ronald C |last3=Smentek |first3=Lidia |date=May 2004 |title=Brian Garner Wybourne |url=https://physicstoday.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1768682 |journal=Physics Today |volume=57 |issue=5 |pages=77 |doi=10.1063/1.1768682 |access-date=2022-10-14|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Born in [[Morrinsville]] in 1935, Wybourne attended [[University of Canterbury|Canterbury University College]], graduating with an [[MSc]] with second-class honours in 1958 and a [[PhD]] in 1960.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university25.html |title=NZ university graduates 1871–1960: Wi–Z |accessdate=4 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Wybourne |first=B. |year=1960 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=An analysis of the solid-state spectra of trivalent rare earth ions |publisher=UC Research Repository, University of Canterbury |hdl=10092/8078 |doi=10.26021/7843 |url=https://ir.canterbury.ac.nz/handle/10092/8078}}</ref>

After post-doctoral research positions at [[Johns Hopkins University]] and [[Argonne National Laboratory]] in the United States, Wybourne returned to the [[University of Canterbury]] in 1966 to take up a professorship in physics, at the age of 31.<ref name="RSNZ obit">{{cite web |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/publications/reports/yearbooks/year2004/obituaries/brian-wybourne/ |title=Brian Garner Wybourne |year=2004 |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |accessdate=4 October 2014 |first=Phil |last=Butler}}</ref> Notable doctoral students of Wybourne at Canterbury include [[Timothy Haskell]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Haskell |first=T. G. |title=The group theory of the harmonic oscillator with applications in physics |date=1972 |access-date=24 Jan 2025 |degree=PhD |publisher=UC Research Repository, [[University of Canterbury]] |url=https://hdl.handle.net/10092/13410 |doi=10.26021/8330}}</ref> 

He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1970,<ref>{{cite web |title=The Academy: V–Z |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/fellows-1919-present/v-z/ |accessdate=4 October 2014 |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand}}</ref> and the same year he won the society's [[Hector Medal]], the highest award in New Zealand science at that time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/hector-medal/recipients/ |title=Hector Medal |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |accessdate=4 October 2014}}</ref>

He served as the head of the physics department from December 1982 to November 1989.<ref>{{cite conference |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261178736 |title=Brian Wybourne: his life at Canterbury |first=Philip H. |last=Butler |date=2006 |editor1-last=King |editor1-first=R.C. |editor2-last=Bylicki |editor2-first=M. |editor3-last=Karwowski |editor3-first=J. |book-title=Symmetry, Spectroscopy and SCHUR: Proceedings of the Prof. Brian G. Wybourne Commemorative Meeting, 12–14 June 2005 |publisher=N. Copernicus University Press |location=Toruń |pages=3–9 |accessdate=4 October 2014}}</ref>  In 1991 he was a visiting professor at the [[Nicholas Copernicus University]] in [[Toruń]], [[Poland]], and decided to remain there permanently.<ref name="RSNZ obit" /> 

Wybourne was appointed to a professorship in the [[Nicholas Copernicus University]] Institute of Physics in 1993. In 2003 he received an award from the Polish Minister of Education for his outstanding contribution to science. A month later he unexpectedly died of a stroke. In his 13 years in Poland Wybourne published 80 scientific papers.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Symmetry, Spectroscopy, and SCHUR |publisher=Nicolaus Copernicus University Press |year=2006 |editor-last=King |editor-first=Ronald C |location=Torun |pages=15 |chapter=3 The Polish Odyssey of Brian G. Wybourne |access-date=2022-10-14 |editor-last2=Bylick |editor-first2=Miroslaw |editor-last3=Karwowski |editor-first3=Jacek |chapter-url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261180565}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=B G Wybourne's research while affiliated with Nicolaus Copernicus University and other places |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/B-G-Wybourne-37170905 |access-date=2022-10-14 |website=ResearchGate}}</ref>

Wybourne's time in Poland was chronicled in ''[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261180565_The_Polish_Odyssey_of_Brian_G_Wybourne The Polish Odyssey of Brian G. Wybourne],'' written by his colleague at [[Nicholas Copernicus University]], [https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Jacek-Karwowski Jacek Karwowski].
